program_name: Master in Smart Technologies for Sports and Health
teaching_language: Fully English. This is a monolingual English-taught programme — 'Courses will be taught in English' (brochure 'At a glance') and 'The official teaching language is English' (admission information). There is NO trilingual (IT/DE/EN) component: no Italian or German course appears in the study plan and no second or third teaching language is defined. Verification against the published 2026/27 course offering confirms the English tag on the courses that carry a language label: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (9 CP, EN), Foundations of Physical Activity and Health (6 CP, EN), Embedded and Software Systems (6 CP, EN), Security and Privacy in Connected Sports and Health Systems (6 CP, EN), Human Biomechanics for Physical Assistive Robots (6 CP, EN), Wearable Electronics (6 CP, EN), Materials and Technologies for Biomimetic Systems (6 CP, EN), Sensors and Electronic Systems for Sports and Health (12 CP, EN), Humans and Systems (12 CP, EN), Robotic Systems for Sports and Health (12 CP, EN). A few entries in that listing (Bionic Limbs, Introduction to Bioengineering, the 1 CP Seminar) carry no explicit language tag in the course-offering view, but the programme's official monolingual status makes English the operative language throughout. The programme is explicitly marketed as internationally open: 'taught entirely in English with teaching staff as well as students coming from Italy, Europe and the entire world.'
campus: NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano (Faculty of Engineering campus at the South Tyrolean science and technology park, Bruno-Buozzi-Straße 1 / via Bruno Buozzi 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano). Teaching, laboratory and project activities all take place at this campus. Associated laboratories accessible to students: Electronics engineering — Flexible Electronics Lab, Media Interaction Lab, Sensing Technologies Lab, Photonics and Optoelectronics Lab; Automation and Robotics engineering — Human-Centered Technologies and Machine Intelligence Lab, FIRST Field Robotics South-Tyrol Lab; Computer Engineering — Collective Design and Ideation Lab, Physical Computing Lab, User Experience Lab, Data Driven Artificial Intelligence Lab, Cybersecurity Laboratory.
degree_class: LM-32 (Ingegneria informatica / Computer Engineering). 120 ECTS, 2 years, full-time. Graduates may sit the Italian state examination for the profession of 'Ingegnere dell'informazione' (Information Engineer) and, on passing, join the Ordine degli Ingegneri (Italian Chamber of Engineers) — Section A.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered and the 2026/27 intake has already run. Both the Early Bird ranking list and the Late Application ranking list for a.y. 2026/27 have been published and signed, with students actually admitted in each (7 EU + 5 non-EU in Early Bird, 3 EU in Late). As of the verification date the programme additionally has an Additional Application Session open (18/08 - 04/09/2026, EU citizens only), and the official Additional Application Session page lists 'Master in Smart Technologies for Sports and Health (Application possible)'. Note that, unlike some other unibz programmes, this programme's page does not display a 'Courses will definitely be starting' status box; the evidence of actual operation comes from the signed ranking lists and the published 2026/27 course offering.
is_new_programme: Yes — a recently launched programme. The official course-contents document is headed 'Coorti dal 2025-2026' ('cohorts from 2025-2026'), and the study-career Excel template published for the admission procedure is named 'excel-file-Smart-Technologies-for-Sports-and-Health-2025-26.xlsx', both indicating that the FIRST INTAKE was academic year 2025/26. Academic year 2026/27 is therefore the programme's second intake. [uncertain] — unibz does not publish an explicit 'new programme, first intake YYYY' statement for this course; the 2025/26 first-cohort conclusion is inferred from the cohort label on the course-description PDF and the file naming, not from a direct declaration.
majors_tracks_study_plans: No majors, no tracks and no alternative study plans — a single 120 ECTS study plan for all students, full-time only. Internal choice happens through two mechanisms in year 2: (1) 'Specialisation topics' — students pick TWO of four 6 CP courses: Human Biomechanics for Physical Assistive Robots, Wearable Electronics, Materials and Technologies for Biomimetic Systems, Bionic Limbs; and (2) 12 CP of Free Choice. Structure by phase: first part 45 ECTS (targeted knowledge in computer engineering, bioengineering and biomedical sciences, to homogenise incoming backgrounds); second part 52 ECTS (embedded systems and cognitive robotic systems, plus up to 12 ECTS of electives, lab-heavy and with experiential learning alongside companies); third part 20 ECTS (master thesis, writable in house at unibz or with local/international companies). Full study plan — Year 1: Foundations of Physical Activity and Health 6 CP; Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning 9 CP; Humans and Systems 12 CP (M-1 Human-System Interaction 6 CP, M-2 Sports and Health Behaviour and System Recommendation 6 CP); Introduction to Bioengineering 12 CP (M-1 Bioengineering 6 CP, M-2 Biosignal Processing 6 CP); Sensors and Electronic Systems for Sports and Health 12 CP (M-1 Sensors for Biosignals 6 CP, M-2 Electronic Systems for Sports and Health 6 CP); Robotic Systems for Sports and Health 12 CP (M-1 Cognitive Robotics 6 CP, M-2 Socially-Aware Robot Assistants 6 CP). Year 2: Embedded and Software Systems 6 CP; Security and Privacy in Connected Sports and Health Systems 6 CP; two Specialisation topics 6 CP each; Free Choice 12 CP; Seminar 1 CP; Master Thesis 20 CP. Internship is OPTIONAL, with a maximum of 300 hours (there is no compulsory internship, in contrast with some other unibz programmes). Degree Course Director: Prof. Angelika Peer.
english_only_accessibility: OPEN — this is one of the genuinely English-accessible unibz programmes and the single most important contrast with the trilingual Bolzano bachelors. The only language requirement is English at B2 for entry; no Italian and no German is required at any point of the admission procedure, and no second or third language exists in the programme's language rules. Empirical confirmation from the published 2026/27 Early Bird ranking list: under the heading for applicants excluded on language grounds the document records 'No candidate failed to meet the language requirements' — i.e. zero language-based exclusions, against 26 language exclusions in the trilingual Bachelor in Computer Science at the same faculty. Non-EU applicants living abroad were actually admitted (5 of 7 available places in the Early Bird session), which for the trilingual bachelors did not happen at all. The practical filters here are academic rather than linguistic: the 36 ECTS computing/engineering plus 18 ECTS mathematics/physics curricular prerequisites, and the 24/30 grade-average threshold (which, if missed, is remediable by interview rather than fatal).
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with a merit-based ranking list, decided by documentary evaluation of the applicant's study career. There is NO entrance exam, no TOLC, no SAT, no CENT-S, no portfolio and no motivation letter. Scoring is fully documentary (up to 40 points). A conditional interview instrument exists: applicants whose previous-studies grade average is below 24/30 are invited to an online interview in English and are admitted only if they pass it. Two eliminatory prerequisites gate the ranking rather than scoring in it — the curricular ECTS requirements and the English B2 certificate. Separate ranking lists are drawn for (a) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (b) non-EU citizens living abroad. Admission Committee for 2026/27: President Prof. Dr. Angelika Peer; members Dr. Floriano Zini and Dr. Pietro Ibba.
academic_requirements: ADMISSION TITLE — one of: a bachelor degree or an equivalent qualification under previous regulations obtained in Italy; or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. A foreign degree must evidence at least 180 ECTS and must give access to a master programme in the awarding country (both points must appear in the Diploma Supplement). CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS, obtainable through bachelor degrees, master degrees OR single subject courses (so gaps can be filled with standalone university courses): (A) at least 36 ECTS in the scientific-disciplinary sectors INFO-01/A (ex INF/01) Computer Science; IINF-05/A (ex ING-INF/05) Information Processing Systems; IINF-01/A (ex ING-INF/01) Electronic Engineering; IINF-04/A (ex ING-INF/04) Systems and Control Engineering; IIND-02/A (ex ING-IND/13) Applied Mechanics; IIND-08/A (ex ING-IND/32) Power Electronic Converters, Electrical Machines and Drives; IIET-01/A (ex ING-IND/31) Electrical Engineering. (B) at least 18 ECTS in MATH-01/A (ex MAT/01) Mathematical Logic; MATH-02/A (ex MAT/02) Algebra; MATH-02/B (ex MAT/03) Geometry; MATH-03/A (ex MAT/05) Mathematical Analysis; MATH-03/B (ex MAT/06) Probability and Mathematical Statistics; MATH-04/A (ex MAT/07) Mathematical Physics; MATH-05/A (ex MAT/08) Numerical Analysis; MATH-06/A (ex MAT/09) Operational Research; PHYS-01/A (ex FIS/01 and FIS/04) Experimental Physics of Fundamental Interactions and Applications; PHYS-02/A (ex FIS/02 and FIS/04) Theoretical Physics of Fundamental Interactions, Models, Mathematical Methods and Applications; PHYS-03/A (ex FIS/01 and FIS/03) Experimental Physics of Matter and Applications; PHYS-04/A (ex FIS/02 and FIS/03) Theoretical Physics of Matter, Models, Mathematical Methods and Applications. Both the new 2024-reform SSD codes and their old equivalents are given by unibz itself. For candidates holding a foreign qualification, 'the verification of the curricular requirements is based on the specific contents of the educational activities' — i.e. course content, not code matching, decides, which is why the structured study-career Excel upload asks for course names in the original language plus English translation, credits and (for Italian degrees) SSD. PERSONAL PREPARATION: an adequate personal preparation with a mark average of at least 24/30 in previous university studies; below that, the Admission Committee decides on the applicant's adequacy via interview. LANGUAGE: English B2 (see language_requirements). Possession of the curricular requirements gives NO score — it is a pure admission prerequisite. National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 study programmes, which must not belong to the same class (e.g. not LM-18/LM-18) and must differ in at least 2/3 of course contents.
entry_exam_or_test: NONE. There is no unibz aptitude test, no TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT/GRE/GMAT and no written subject test for this programme. The only examinations connected with admission are (a) the optional unibz Language Centre English exams, for applicants who choose that route to prove B2 — Early Bird session: online exams 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late session: online exams 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026); and (b) the conditional online interview in English for applicants below the 24/30 average (see 'interview'). IMPORTANT for the currently open Additional Application Session: 'the unibz Language Centre does not offer language exams for this application session' — applicants in the 18/08-04/09/2026 window must bring an external certificate, and unibz explicitly recommends LanguageCert, TOEFL or IELTS because results arrive quickly.
selection_scoring: Documentary scoring on a maximum of 40 points, based entirely on the study career uploaded in the portal. (1) ADMISSION TITLE — up to 30 points, based on the grade average obtained at the time of application. (2) ORIGIN OF THE DEGREE — up to 10 points, based on the awarding university's position in the Webometrics Ranking of World Universities: 10 points for positions 1-100; 8 points for 101-500; 5 points for 501-1000; 3 points for 1001-2000; 1 point for 2001-3000; 0 points from 3001 onwards. (3) Possession of the curricular requirements scores ZERO points — it is an admission prerequisite only. (4) The English language certificate scores ZERO points — also a prerequisite only. THRESHOLD: candidates must have an average mark of at least 24/30; candidates below that must pass an online interview in English demonstrating their knowledge, and are otherwise excluded. There is no published minimum total-point threshold beyond this. COMPETITION LEVEL 2026/27 — low relative to capacity: Early Bird admitted 7 EU/equivalent against 10 EU places and 5 non-EU against 7 non-EU places; the Late session admitted 3 EU against 8 places. Both ranking lists state 'There is no waiting list, all candidates are either excluded or admitted', meaning capacity was not binding and effectively every qualifying applicant was taken. Note the Webometrics scale is markedly more generous here than in the sister programmes (Master in Software Engineering / Computing for Data Science award only 3/2/1 points for the 1001-3000 bands and nothing above); this programme awards up to 10 points and rewards top-100 and top-500 universities heavily.
bonus_points: The only ranking bonus is the Webometrics university-origin score, worth up to 10 of the 40 available points: 10 points (rank 1-100), 8 points (101-500), 5 points (501-1000), 3 points (1001-2000), 1 point (2001-3000), 0 points (3001+). There is NO GMAT/GRE bonus (that belongs to the Master in Accounting and Finance), no startup-project presentation bonus (Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation), no extracurricular-activities bonus (that is a bachelor-level instrument) and no bonus for language certificates above B2 — the English certificate is explicitly stated to give no score. Practical consequence for applicants from lower-ranked universities: the maximum realistic loss is 10 points out of 40, so a strong grade average remains the dominant factor.
portfolio_and_materials: No portfolio, no motivation letter, no video, no project proposal, no reference letters and no CV are required. The single structured upload that carries real weight is the STUDY CAREER EXCEL FILE, which is mandatory: applicants download the .xls template plus a filled-in PDF example from the application portal (the university also publishes the worked example at /assets/Documents/Faculty-Computer-Science/2025-02-25-Master-in-Smart-Technologies-for-Sports-and-Health-admission-procedure.pdf, and the template at /assets/Documents/Faculty-Computer-Science/excel-file-Smart-Technologies-for-Sports-and-Health-2025-26.xlsx). Both worksheets must be completed — tab 'ADMISSION TITLE (BACHELOR)' and tab 'OTHER UNIVERSITY COURSES' — and the file must be uploaded as an EXCEL file, not as a PDF of it. Formatting rules from the official example: save the file as surname-name.xls; do not change the structure of the file, only add rows where a disciplinary area needs more space; state your average mark plus the minimum passing grade and maximum possible grade; if a final grade / voto di laurea / GPA / CGPA exists you MUST state it together with its minimum and maximum thresholds; list ALL courses taken during the bachelor; group courses under the disciplinary-area headings used in the template (Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Other disciplines); for courses taken at an Italian university the SSD must be given; if two grading scales were used (e.g. theory vs labs) they must be declared separately as Grading Scale 1 and Grading Scale 2 and each course tagged 'GS 1' or 'GS 2'; use your local credits; in the 'Other university courses' tab also give total class hours, awarding university and its town/country, and do not repeat courses already listed in the admission-title tab. Additionally: applicants who graduated in ITALY must self-declare the exams passed, or be excluded; applicants who graduated ABROAD must upload their academic transcript, or be excluded. No file-size or page limits are published for this programme.
interview: Yes — a conditional, remedial online interview, not a universal one. Only applicants whose previous-studies grade average is BELOW 24/30 are invited; they must 'pass an online interview in English in which they demonstrate their knowledge' to be admitted. Published dates for 2026/27: Early Bird session 18/05/2026; Late session 27/07/2026; second/additional session 'to be defined' in the admission-information document. Evidence that the mechanism is real and generously applied: in the Early Bird session three EU/equivalent applicants (IDs 153310, 152254, 153180) and three non-EU applicants (IDs 155080, 151955, 154780) were below threshold, all attended, all passed and all entered the ranking list — six of the twelve Early Bird admissions came through the interview route. In the Late session, by contrast, both below-threshold candidates (IDs 156880, 142515) failed to attend and were consequently excluded — showing that non-attendance is fatal. [uncertain] — the Early Bird ranking list is internally inconsistent about the interview date: its admission-criteria header refers to 'the interview of May 11, 2026' while its results section twice refers to the interview 'scheduled to take place May 18' and 'the interview of May 18, 2026'; the admission-information PDF and brochure both give 18/05/2026, so 18 May is the better-supported date and 11 May appears to be an editing error.
conditional_admission: Yes, with a 120 ECTS threshold. Applicants who have not yet graduated at the time of application may apply if they have acquired at least 120 credit points (ECTS); they are then admitted CONDITIONALLY and must submit the diploma by the enrolment deadline (13/10/2026, noon). If the qualification is achieved AFTER the enrolment deadline, the applicant cannot enrol and loses the place, which passes to the next applicant on the ranking list — unibz explicitly advises such applicants NOT to pay the tuition fees to secure the place. A late-enrolment request may then be submitted to the Rector and, ONLY if study places are still available, enrolment is possible by 11 DECEMBER 2026. Both 2026/27 ranking lists mark provisionally admitted applicants with an asterisk covering two distinct situations: (a) applicants who have not concluded their bachelor's degree, and (b) applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not yet uploaded their diploma, who remain provisionally admitted until the study title is verified. A third layer applies to non-EU applicants: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.' Admission with reservation is only lifted once the required documents are uploaded and the title is deemed eligible; if it is not, enrolment is impossible and the applicant is excluded — and exclusion by Rector's decree is possible even after enrolment. Note the 140 ECTS variant mentioned in the field schema belongs to the Master in Data Analytics, not to this programme, which uses the standard 120 ECTS figure.
ofa_rules: Not applicable. OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) is a bachelor-level instrument at unibz, used for example in Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics and Tourism Sport and Event Management after a compulsory mathematics test, and in the Bachelor in Computer Science on the basis of secondary-school mathematics grades. Neither the admission-information document, the brochure nor either 2026/27 ranking list for this master mentions OFA, an additional learning obligation or any catch-up test, and no asterisk in the ranking lists denotes OFA (the asterisks here denote provisional admission pending the bachelor diploma or foreign-title verification). At master level the equivalent function is served by the eliminatory curricular requirements (36 + 18 ECTS) and, for weak averages, by the remedial interview: a candidate who lacks the prerequisite credits is not admitted with a debt, but simply not admitted.
language_requirements: Single-language regime: 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' ENTRY LEVEL (to gain admission): English B2 on the Common European Framework of Reference. That is the entire requirement — no Italian, no German, no second language and no third language. The rule is ELIMINATORY (failure to certify means exclusion from the admission procedure, not a lower rank) but it carries NO SCORE ('The certificate of English language proficiency does not give a score but is an admission prerequisite'). Proficiency is demonstrated in the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', after creating an application under 'create/manage applications'. Administrative distinction: if the final certificate was awarded by an Italian public institution a self-declaration is required; if awarded by a foreign public institution a scanned copy of the original must be uploaded. Certificates that cannot be uploaded may be e-mailed as PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. Free Language Centre courses remain available to enrolled students (intensive courses before the first term and between terms, plus 40-hour courses during the semesters), but for this programme they are an optional benefit rather than a requirement — the university encourages plurilingualism and students may voluntarily pick up Italian or German. Warning specific to the currently open Additional Application Session: no Language Centre language exams are offered for that session, so an external certificate is the only route; unibz recommends LanguageCert, TOEFL or IELTS for speed.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: English B2. 2nd language: none required. 3rd language: none required. The 'position' logic used by the trilingual unibz programmes (where the 1st language is the applicant's strongest and levels are assigned by position rather than by language) does not apply here, because the programme defines exactly one teaching language. In schema shorthand the pattern is B2 / none / none, which is the most permissive entry profile at unibz — one full step below the B2/B2/none of the trilingual engineering bachelors and two below the C1/B2/none of programmes such as Public Policy and Innovative Governance or Accounting and Finance. Note that unibz Language Centre exams for this purpose are offered at B2 level, and that the two recognised 'automatic' routes (English-medium high school, or an English-taught bachelor/master degree) are recognised as C1, comfortably clearing the B2 bar.
exit_levels: No language exit requirement is published for this programme. Neither the admission-information document nor the brochure nor the ranking lists define an exit level, and the Language Centre's 'study in three languages' page states entry-level rules only, specifying no mandatory graduation proficiency levels for any programme type including English-taught masters. This contrasts sharply with the trilingual bachelors, where C1/C1/B2 is a hard graduation gate. Practically, a student admitted with English B2 has no further certified-language hurdle before graduating from this master. [uncertain] — this is an argument from the absence of any published requirement across all official programme documents rather than from an explicit unibz statement that no exit level exists; the Faculty's study regulations (regolamento didattico), which were not located in English, are the only place a residual requirement could hide.
third_language_exam_threshold: Not applicable. The B1-in-the-third-language rule (the minimum needed to sit curricular examinations held in that language, and the mid-January English B1 deadline for students whose third language is English) exists only in the trilingual programmes. This master has a single teaching language, so there is no second or third language, no placement test for a third language and no B1 threshold of any kind. The admission-information document does carry the boilerplate line 'For information on studying in three languages also visit the following page', but that is a generic university-wide link and imposes no requirement on this programme. Students may of course learn Italian or German voluntarily through the free Language Centre courses.
proof_pathways: Four recognised pathways to prove English B2, identical in structure to the rest of unibz but applied to one language only. (1) THE MAIN TEACHING LANGUAGE OF YOUR FINAL HIGH SCHOOL YEAR, if English — recognised as C1. For foreign qualifications, if the main teaching language is not clearly stated on the high school diploma, a letter/document issued by the high school stating the medium of instruction must also be uploaded. (2) A BACHELOR OR MASTER DEGREE IN ENGLISH — recognised as C1. unibz graduates upload the language certificates obtained and/or declare that they passed Language Centre exams (B2, B2+ or C1). For foreign qualifications, if the teaching language is not clearly stated on the university degree, a letter/document issued by the university stating the medium of instruction during the studies must also be uploaded. This is the most common route for the typical applicant to this programme, who holds an English-taught engineering or computer science bachelor. (3) A RECOGNISED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE from the official unibz list; if it cannot be uploaded it may be sent by e-mail as a PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) LANGUAGE EXAMS ORGANISED BY THE UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE, registered online through the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after filling out the application. Registration windows and exam dates for 2026/27 — Early Bird: exams 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late: exams 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). If an application is started outside a registration period, the applicant must return to the portal during one of these periods to register. CRITICAL EXCEPTION: pathway (4) is NOT available for the Additional Application Session (18/08-04/09/2026) — the Language Centre offers no exams for that session, and unibz recommends obtaining a LanguageCert, TOEFL or IELTS certificate instead because those results are published quickly.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026, 'Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants' (published trilingually as Beschluss des Universitätsrates / Delibera del Consiglio dell'Università / Resolution of the University Council 16/2026). General dispositions: (1) the certificate must include the assessment of ALL FOUR SKILLS and must be issued by the certification organisation itself; (2) it must indicate adequate performance in all skills as an overall grade, or the detailed assessment must appear on the certificate itself or in appropriate documentation from the certification organisation; (3) if no overall result and/or level is stated, THE LOWEST LEVEL REACHED IN ANY SUB-SKILL is decisive for determining the level, provided that part of the examination was passed; (4) there is NO COMPENSATION for failed parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless the certification organisation itself provides them; (5) certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online 'HOME EDITION' exam are NOT recognised, except those explicitly flagged in the list; (6) certificates covering single skills issued by different certification organisations are not accepted; (7) certificates of participation in language courses, end-of-course tests and exams issued by private educational institutions, and placement-test results, are not recognised; (8) certificates issued by individual lecturers, lettori or language teachers are not recognised; (9) DAAD certificates are NOT recognised. VALIDITY: international language certificates must have been obtained within the last FIVE YEARS before submission — certificates issued from 1 January of the fifth preceding year are valid for the whole of that year. Items listed in the 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' section have UNLIMITED validity. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf
application_deadline_eu: Three sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO normalised below). All deadlines are BY NOON LOCAL TIME. (1) EARLY BIRD APPLICATION: 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. (2) LATE APPLICATION (EU citizens only): 28/05/2026 - 08/07/2026 = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08. (3) ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU citizens only, opened by the Faculty in August/September only where places remain): 18/08/2026 - 04/09/2026 = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04 — and this session IS confirmed open for this specific programme on the official Additional Application Session page ('Master in Smart Technologies for Sports and Health — Application possible'). EU applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and an applicant excluded in the first session may apply again in the second. As of the verification date (2026-08-29) the Early Bird and Late sessions have closed with ranking lists published; only the Additional Application Session remains open, closing 2026-09-04 at noon.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the EARLY BIRD APPLICATION, 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Non-EU citizens living abroad are excluded from the Late Application and from the Additional Application Session (both are explicitly EU-only), pay a non-refundable €50 application fee, are ranked on a separate ranking list against a separate 7-place quota, and must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) to obtain the study visa. For a Turkish or other non-EU applicant living abroad and targeting 2026/27, this window has closed and the next opportunity is the Early Bird window of the following academic year — unless the applicant qualifies for parity of treatment (see parity_of_treatment).
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU applicants, and this is the decisive third category for Turkish and other non-EU applicants. (1) Citizens of NORWAY, ICELAND, LIECHTENSTEIN, SWITZERLAND, SAN MARINO and the VATICAN CITY STATE. (2) Non-EU citizens holding a valid Italian permit to stay ('permesso di soggiorno') under article 39, paragraph 5 of Decree no. 286 of 25/07/1998 — issued for WORK, FAMILY REASONS, POLITICAL OR HUMANITARIAN ASYLUM, or RELIGIOUS REASONS. Such applicants apply directly to the University and must upload a copy of the valid permit; if the permit has expired, a renewal request must be attached. A PERMIT TO STAY FOR STUDY REASONS OR A VISA FOR TOURISM IS NOT VALID. Critical procedural warning, restated in both the admission-information document and the signed ranking lists: 'if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin' — the ranking list phrases it as 'If you have declared to be resident in Italy but have not attached to your application a copy of your valid residence permit for Italy ... you are ranked together with the non-EU citizen resident abroad.' The consequences of that misclassification are concrete: loss of access to the Late and Additional sessions, movement onto the 7-place non-EU list instead of the 18-place EU list, and a €50 fee. Practically, a non-EU national already living in Italy on a work or family permit gets the full EU treatment on this programme, including the currently open Additional Application Session.
places_quotas: Three separate quotas for 2026/27, totalling '18 EU + 7 non-EU' as summarised in the brochure and on the programme page. EU CITIZENS AND CITIZENS GIVEN PARITY OF TREATMENT: Early Bird Application 10 places; Late Application 8 places (10 + 8 = 18). NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD: Early Bird Application 7 places, with no non-EU quota in any later session. CARRY-OVER RULE: for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only, any places remaining from the Early Bird application are offered in the Late Application. ACTUAL 2026/27 UPTAKE, from the signed ranking lists: Early Bird admitted 7 EU/equivalent (against 10 places) and 5 non-EU living abroad (against 7 places); the Late Application admitted 3 EU/equivalent (against 8 places). Total admitted across both published sessions: 15 against 25 advertised places. Both ranking lists state 'There is no waiting list, all candidates are either excluded or admitted' — i.e. demand did not exhaust capacity in either session, which is why an Additional Application Session was opened. No separate numeric quota is published for the Additional Application Session; it draws on the remaining unfilled EU places.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: EARLY BIRD: ranking lists published by 27/05/2026; payment of the 1st instalment of tuition fees (€600 — this is what secures the place) by 05/06/2026 noon; enrolment from 10/07/2026 to 13/10/2026 noon. LATE APPLICATION: ranking lists published by 30/07/2026; 1st instalment by 06/08/2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 13/10/2026 noon. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION: ranking lists published by 18/09/2026; 1st instalment by 25/09/2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 13/10/2026 noon. Note that the enrolment window closes on the SAME date (13/10/2026) for all three sessions, which is markedly later than the bachelor pattern (06/08/2026) and gives non-EU admitted students more room for visa processing. LATE ENROLMENT: applicants who obtain their qualification after the enrolment deadline may submit a late-enrolment request to the Rector and, only if places remain, enrol by 11/12/2026. Missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline means automatic exclusion and the place passes to the next applicant on the ranking list. An applicant admitted to more than one programme may secure up to 2 places by paying the instalment twice, thereby renouncing admission to the others. Paying the fees does NOT confer student status — only enrolment does — and there is no refund if you pay but do not enrol, except for non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country. Appeals against the ranking decree may be lodged with the Bozen-Bolzano Administrative Court within 60 days of notification or publication.

required_documents: AT APPLICATION, online via the Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): (1) an account plus a valid ID card or passport, FRONT AND BACK — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; (2) the completed online form; (3) THE STUDY CAREER EXCEL FILE — both worksheets ('Admission title' and 'Other university courses') filled in and uploaded as an excel file, downloaded together with a filled-in PDF example from the portal; (4) if you graduated in Italy: self-declaration of the exams passed, otherwise exclusion; (5) if you graduated abroad: your academic transcript, otherwise exclusion; (6) proof of English B2 — an uploaded certificate, a self-declaration (Italian public institution) or a scanned original diploma (foreign public institution), or registration for a Language Centre exam; (7) if the qualification was gained abroad, the diploma of the qualification — if not yet held, it is uploaded at enrolment; (8) for non-EU citizens resident in Italy claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid permit to stay, plus a renewal request if expired. Once the application has been sent it CANNOT be modified, and forms filled in but not correctly sent are not taken into consideration. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and result in automatic exclusion from the ranking list. AT ENROLMENT, holders of a foreign university degree must additionally upload: the bachelor degree diploma; an official translation of the degree into Italian (not necessary if documents were issued in German or English); and the DIPLOMA SUPPLEMENT, which must state both that at least 180 ECTS were achieved and that the qualification gives access to a master programme. Depending on the education system, ARDI and/or CIMEA statements are also required (see credential_recognition). Students transferring from another Italian university must submit a copy of the transfer application to the Student Office at the beginning of the academic year. Non-EU students must hand in a copy of the residence permit to the Student Office, in person or by e-mail, once obtained.
application_fee: €50, payable only by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. It is described as an administration fee and is explicitly NON-REFUNDABLE. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — including non-EU nationals holding a qualifying Italian permit to stay for work, family, asylum or religious reasons — pay no application fee.
tuition_or_fees_link: Total tuition fees are €1,200 per year, in two instalments: 1st instalment €600, which INCLUDES the €16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo) and is the payment that secures the study place after admission; 2nd instalment €600, to be paid by March of the following year. Delayed payment of the second instalment results in a fine. Unpaid fees block exam-taking and any transfer to another university or study programme. No reimbursement if you drop out, interrupt your studies or are excluded. EXEMPTIONS: students with a disability recognised under article 3, paragraph 1 of Law no. 104/1992, or with a disability of 66% or more (the disability certificate issued by the health authorities must be handed in at the beginning of the academic year); and foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government. Students who receive a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to a REFUND of the tuition fees paid. Fees information: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ and the programme's own admission-information PDF at https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/master-in-smart-technologies-for-sports-and-health_admission-information_en_GB.pdf
scholarships_grants: The main route is the income-based provincial study grant from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano, administered by the Office for the Right to Study (Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario) and applied for online through the provincial e-government service, with assistance available from the South Tyrolean Students Association. The province offers three instruments: ordinary study grants, merit scholarships, and grants for fostering postgraduate studies. Grant recipients also receive a refund of the unibz tuition fees. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption' — a newly arrived non-EU first-year student is therefore effectively ineligible in year one and should budget accordingly (the same year-one gap that the visa's €24,000 proof-of-means requirement already assumes). Other funding routes listed by unibz: Italian Government scholarships (which also carry a tuition-fee exemption), Austrian student grants, German BAföG, and bank loans through Italian financial institutions; the Municipality of Meran scholarship is restricted to Food and Enogastronomy students and does not apply here. unibz itself grants tuition-fee exemptions (disability, Italian government scholarship holders) rather than cash scholarships. No programme-specific scholarship is published for the Master in Smart Technologies for Sports and Health. Contact: study@unibz.it, +39 0471 012900. Reference page: https://guide.unibz.it/en/life-on-campus/study-grants
credential_recognition: At enrolment, holders of a foreign university degree must upload the bachelor degree diploma, an official translation into Italian (not necessary if the documents were issued in German or English), and the Diploma Supplement stating both that at least 180 ECTS were achieved and that the qualification gives access to a master programme. Then, depending on the education system: (a) EU COUNTRIES, SWITZERLAND, NORWAY, ICELAND, LIECHTENSTEIN — a Statement of Correspondence of the bachelor degree, downloaded from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database Italy, https://ardi.cimea.it/en). (b) NON-EU COUNTRIES THAT ARE SIGNATORIES TO THE LISBON CONVENTION — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA (Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence). (c) NON-EU COUNTRIES THAT ARE NOT SIGNATORIES TO THE LISBON CONVENTION — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Türkiye is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish applicants normally fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification. Admission remains UNDER RESERVATION until these documents are uploaded; unibz verifies the foreign qualification during enrolment and may request additional documents; if the access title is deemed eligible the reservation is lifted, otherwise enrolment is not possible and the applicant is excluded — and exclusion by Rector's decree is possible even after enrolment. Note the separate, earlier check on CURRICULAR requirements: for candidates with a foreign qualification, verification of the 36 + 18 ECTS prerequisites 'is based on the specific contents of the educational activities', which is assessed from the study-career Excel file and transcript at the application stage, not from ARDI/CIMEA paperwork. Recognition of credit points from previous university studies is possible only after enrolment and only where the exams taken elsewhere are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz. Signatory list: https://www.enic-naric.net/ ; CIMEA services: https://cimea-diplome.it/
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply to unibz in the Early Bird window only (02/03-28/04/2026, €50 non-refundable fee) → appear on the separate non-EU ranking list (7 places) → if admitted, secure the place by paying the €600 first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon → THEN start the visa application by pre-enrolling on the Universitaly portal of the Italian Ministry of Universities and Research. The Universitaly application is MANDATORY: 'Should you not follow this procedure, your direct online application to unibz will be declared null and void', and only ONE study programme may be selected on Universitaly. The Italian diplomatic-consular authorities in the applicant's country then issue the entry visa for studies/university. Explicit caveats: preliminary admission by unibz does not guarantee obtaining a visa or even an appointment at the Italian representation, since visas are the exclusive responsibility of embassies and consulates; and obtaining a study visa confers no right to complete enrolment. FINANCIAL MEANS for the visa: at least €800 PER MONTH for living costs (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing) in the Bozen-Bolzano area, excluding tuition fees, with a total proof of at least €24,000 FOR A MASTER PROGRAMME (the €36,000 figure applies to bachelor programmes). Health insurance and visa expenses must also be budgeted. AFTER ARRIVAL: within 8 working days of arrival in Italy the residence permit ('permesso di soggiorno') must have been applied for — contact the Advisory Service / Student Support immediately on arrival — and once obtained a copy must be handed in at the Student Office in person or by e-mail. WORK: with a study residence permit, students may work part-time for no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. A further conditionality applies to this cohort: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.' REFUND EXCEPTION: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country are entitled to a refund. The 13/10/2026 enrolment deadline (with possible late enrolment to 11/12/2026 if places remain) gives more visa headroom than the bachelor programmes' August cut-off. Universitaly: https://www.universitaly.it/

uncertainty_notes: Data year: all figures are for academic year 2026/27; the admission-information PDF and brochure both carry 'Subject to change. Latest update: 30.07.2026'. Verified as of 2026-08-29. TIMING: the Early Bird and Late sessions for 2026/27 have CLOSED with signed ranking lists published; the Additional Application Session (18/08-04/09/2026, EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only) is confirmed OPEN for this programme at the verification date and closes 2026-09-04 at noon. (1) INTERVIEW-DATE CONFLICT: the Early Bird ranking list contradicts itself, citing 'the interview of May 11, 2026' in its criteria header but 'May 18' twice in its results section; the admission-information PDF and brochure both say 18/05/2026, so 18 May is treated as correct and 11 May as an editing error. (2) SOURCE DEFECT: the official admission-information PDF contains a truncated sentence, 'Knowledge of the teaching level (at least B2 level of the European reference', which is reproduced verbatim in both ranking lists; the intended meaning ('knowledge of the teaching language at B2 of the CEFR') is unambiguous from the Language requirements section, but the primary source is literally incomplete on this point. The same PDF also duplicates the paragraph 'If you have not yet graduated at the time of application' twice in a row. (3) FIRST-INTAKE YEAR is inferred: the course-contents PDF is scoped to 'Coorti dal 2025-2026' and the study-career Excel template is named for 2025-26, which together indicate a first cohort in 2025/26, but unibz publishes no explicit 'new programme' declaration for this course. Probing the course-offering endpoint for earlier academic years was inconclusive (all years return HTTP 301 redirects). (4) EXIT LANGUAGE LEVEL: no graduation language requirement is published anywhere in this programme's documents, and the Language Centre's trilingual-study page states entry rules only; the conclusion 'no exit requirement' rests on the absence of any published rule rather than on an explicit statement, and the Faculty's Italian-language study regulations were not reviewed. (5) SCHOLARSHIP AMOUNTS are unconfirmed — the unibz study-grants page verified for this programme states no figures at all; the commonly cited €1,680-€6,960 range and any merit-average threshold come from secondary summaries and must be checked against the annual provincial call. (6) NO SEPARATE CALL/MANIFESTO was found in English; a Rector's decree may exist only in the Italian albo. (7) COURSE-LANGUAGE TAGS: three entries in the 2026/27 course-offering listing (Bionic Limbs, Introduction to Bioengineering, the 1 CP Seminar) carry no explicit EN tag in that view; given the programme's declared monolingual English status this is treated as a listing gap, not evidence of another teaching language. (8) NO NUMERIC QUOTA is published for the Additional Application Session — it draws on unfilled EU places (10 of the 18 EU places were still unused after the two published sessions). (9) PDF SLUG TRAP: the programme page URL uses 'sports-health' while the CoursesPDF assets use 'for-sports-and-health'; the short-slug PDF URLs return HTML 404 pages that can be mistaken for valid PDFs by automated fetchers. (10) TURKISH-APPLICANT RELEVANCE: Türkiye's status as a Lisbon Convention signatory (hence ARDI + CIMEA Verification, case (b)) is derived from the convention's membership list, not stated by unibz for this programme. (11) The 140 ECTS conditional-admission threshold and the OFA rules referenced in the field schema belong to other unibz programmes and do not apply here.
